correctness.rationale: Exact argument: mutual congruences force gcd(a,b)=1 and integer M=(F(a)+F(b)-1)/(ab). For a<b, the positive integer r=F(a)/b is smaller than a; the monic quadratic has roots b and r, so (r,a) has the same M and mutual congruences. Descent ends at (1,1), where M=1, contradicting M>1 outside that point. The squarefree n corollary uses the cited product formula, sixth-order root criterion including primes 2 and 3, and a finite graph cycle argument. The checker independently tests exact rational sums and reciprocal conditions for finite ranges only.

value.rationale: An exact zero theorem eliminates the distinct-prime, first-power two-cycle configuration for which the motivating 2026 paper devotes Proposition 1 to a nontrivial quantitative bound; it also gives a new structural necessity for squarefree integer-valued reciprocal-gcd sums: every prime factor is 1 modulo 6 and the prime-support size is at least 3. This is a motivated algebraic obstruction, not a numerical extension or a restatement of the global count. The broader squarefree three-cycle problem remains open within the present argument.
